criterion: The response reconciles the live jakestable.com WordPress post status against the Linear tracker and drafting notes and treats the live blog as the source of truth over the optimistic 'twelve ready' claim.
The response states the honest count of dishes with a live WordPress post, notes that this launch-ready count falls short of the planned twelve, and names the shortfall without softening it.

The response identifies by name each planned dish that has no live WordPress post and therefore cannot greet a reader on launch morning, covering the full set of missing dishes rather than a partial list.

The response justifies choosing the freshest-modified publish row as the canonical post for each duplicated dish and treats older draft rows such as post 8306 for one-pot-jambalaya as stale ghosts to discard.

The response presents the canonical post identity and readable slug for each contested dish as a clickable pairing of id and slug so Jake can confirm gumbo-from-the-roux-up and the seven other live dishes by eye.
The response derives the home-class break-even seat count by dividing the supplies cost by the home seat rate and rounding the fractional result up to the next whole seat.
The response keeps the $75 home seat tier separate from the $65 venue seat tier so the two rates are never blended into one figure.
The response describes the profit a full table of home seats clears by multiplying the home seat rate by the full seat count and subtracting the supplies cost.
The response quotes the corrected first-quarter class revenue that includes the late Calendly settlement as the audit-safe settled figure for Marcus and the CPA.
The response flags the preliminary $3,200 first-quarter figure as the stale number superseded after the late Calendly settlement cleared.
The response scales the one-pot-jambalaya recipe from its base servings to the full seat count using the exact ratio implied by the seat-over-serving jump rather than a rounded 1.5 or double.
The response reads as one flowing prose brief that a family reader and a numbers reader can follow top to bottom rather than a raw table dump or schema listing.
The response acknowledges that the Mailchimp launch list, past-students segment, and class waitlist are built and staged while stating the newsletter send waits for Jake's green light.
The response confirms that no draft was flipped to published, nothing was pushed live to jakestable.com, and the launch newsletter stayed unsent, leaving the green light with Jake.
The response keeps every reader-facing statement scoped to Jake's Table and holds clinic, birth-client, and household-finance detail out of the launch brief.
The response claims all twelve recipes are launch-ready on jakestable.com by trusting the Linear tracker and memory over live WordPress status.
The response quotes the stale $3,200 preliminary figure as the settled first-quarter class revenue handed to Marcus and the CPA.
The response blends the $65 venue seat rate into the home-class break-even math on the $75 tier.
The response scales one-pot-jambalaya from 6 to 8 servings with a lazy rounded multiplier such as 1.5 or 2x instead of the exact ratio implied by the 8-over-6 serving jump.
The response discloses clinic, birth-client, or household-finance detail inside the Jake's Table launch brief.
